sections.heading: Metadata
sections.text:
Metadata helps search engines understand your content better (which can result in better SEO), and allows you to customize how your content is presented on social media, helping you create a more engaging and consistent user experience across various platforms.

The Metadata API in Next.js allows you to modify the `<head>` element of a page. You can configure metadata in two ways:

* **Config-based Metadata**: Export a [static `metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) or a dynamic [`generateMetadata` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#generatemetadata-function) in a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
* **File-based Metadata**: Add static or dynamically generated special files to route segments.

Additionally, you can create dynamic Open Graph Images using JSX and CSS with [imageResponse](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/image-response) constructor.

sections.heading: Analytics and Monitoring
sections.text:
For large applications, Next.js integrates with popular analytics and monitoring tools to help you understand how your application is performing. Learn more in the  [OpenTelemetry](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry) and [Instrumentation](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation) guides.

- [Images](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/images)
  - Optimize your images with the built-in `next/image` component.
- [Fonts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts)
  - Optimize your application's web fonts with the built-in `next/font` loaders.
- [Scripts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/scripts)
  - Optimize 3rd party scripts with the built-in Script component.
- [Metadata](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/metadata)
  - Use the Metadata API to define metadata in any layout or page.
- [Static Assets](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/static-assets)
  - Next.js allows you to serve static files, like images, in the public directory. You can learn how it works here.
- [Bundle Analyzer](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/bundle-analyzer)
  - Analyze the size of your JavaScript bundles using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.
- [Lazy Loading](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/lazy-loading)
  - Lazy load imported libraries and React Components to improve your application's loading performance.
- [Analytics](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/analytics)
  - Measure and track page performance using Next.js Speed Insights
- [Instrumentation](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation)
  - Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app
- [OpenTelemetry](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry)
  - Learn how to instrument your Next.js app with OpenTelemetry.
- [Third Party Libraries](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/third-party-libraries)
  - Optimize the performance of third-party libraries in your application with the `@next/third-parties` package.

---

skills.name: Image Component Optimization
skills.description: Apply Next.js Image component to optimize images through lazy loading and automatic device-based resizing. Use when rendering images in web applications to reduce load time and improve performance.
skills.skill_body: Use the Next.js Image component instead of native tags. The component automatically handles lazy loading and resizes images based on device viewport size. This reduces initial page load and improves rendering performance. ## Objective optimize image delivery and rendering ## Applicable Signals - image rendering required in component - performance optimization goal stated - responsive design requirement present ## Contraindications - using static HTML img tags without optimization requirements - image optimization already handled by CDN or external service - static asset serving without dynamic resizing ## Workflow Steps - Replace native element with Next.js Image component - Configure lazy loading behavior (default: enabled) - Specify or allow automatic device-based image resizing - Verify images load and resize correctly across target devices ## Constraints - Image component must be imported from next/image - Device viewport information must be available at render time - Image dimensions should be specified or inferred ## Cautions - Lazy loading may delay initial image visibility; consider above-the-fold images - Automatic resizing requires browser support for responsive images ## Output Contract - Images load lazily and automatically resize based on device viewport; page performance metrics improve (reduced initial load time, optimized image delivery)

skills.name: Link Component Prefetching
skills.description: Use Next.js Link component to prefetch linked pages in the background for faster page transitions. Apply when navigating between internal pages to improve perceived performance and user experience.
skills.skill_body:
Invoke the Link component for internal page navigation. The component automatically prefetches the target page in the background, reducing perceived latency on transition. Ensure the href points to an internal route; external links should use standard <a> tags instead.

## Objective

accelerate page navigation through background prefetching
## Applicable Signals

- internal route navigation required
- user experience latency concerns
- multi-page application structure

## Contraindications

- linking to external domains
- prefetching would consume unnecessary bandwidth
- user is on slow or metered connection

## Intervention Moves

- replace native <a> tags with Next.js Link component for internal routes
- configure href attribute to target internal page path
- allow component to handle prefetching automatically

## Constraints

- Link component must wrap internal routes only
- href must point to valid internal page path
- prefetching occurs automatically; no manual configuration required

## Cautions

- External links should use standard <a> tags to avoid prefetch overhead
- Consider user bandwidth constraints before enabling prefetching at scale

## Output Contract

- Linked pages prefetch in background; page transitions appear instantaneous or near-instantaneous to user

skills.name: Script Loading Control
skills.description: Use Next.js Script component to manage loading strategy and execution timing of third-party scripts. Prevents blocking the main thread and optimizes script execution order when integrating external scripts.
skills.skill_body:
Apply the Next.js Script component to third-party scripts. Configure the loading strategy (e.g., async, defer, or on-demand) to ensure scripts do not block page rendering. Verify that the page remains interactive during script loading.

## Objective

control third-party script loading and execution timing
## Applicable Signals

- third-party script integration required
- page interactivity during script load is a concern
- script execution order matters

## Contraindications

- script is critical for initial page render
- using inline scripts that must execute synchronously
- script has no external dependencies and must run before page interaction

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the third-party script and its execution requirements
- Select appropriate loading strategy (async, defer, or on-demand)
- Wrap script in Next.js Script component with chosen strategy
- Verify page remains interactive during script loading
- Monitor script execution order and dependencies

## Constraints

- Script component must be used instead of native <script> tags for optimization benefits
- Loading strategy must be explicitly chosen based on script criticality

## Cautions

- Verify that deferred or async scripts do not cause race conditions with dependent code
- Test page interactivity metrics to confirm non-blocking behavior

## Output Contract

- Third-party scripts load asynchronously without blocking the main thread
- Page remains interactive during script loading
- Script execution timing is controlled and predictable
